nm_la_cueva_canyon_upper.blurb: Upper La Cueva Canyon is on the west side of the Sandia Mountains above Albuquerque, with the La Luz Trail running up through it. Trad dominates, with a set of alpine routes and only a handful of sport and top-rope lines. Grades start around 5.6 and run to 5.12, with the most climbs at 5.10 and 5.11 and a solid base of 5.7 to 5.9. The canyon has a dense concentration of routes on granite faces, and the approaches tend to be easier than at many other Sandia crags. Hole in the Wall holds the most climbs, followed by My Secret Garden, Torreon and The Thumb. This is self-protected climbing where you place your own gear and build your own anchors. Climbing in the Sandias runs year round, though violent thunderstorms often arrive on summer afternoons.

bc_victoria.blurb: Victoria's climbing is a handful of crags around the city on southern Vancouver Island. Sport routes make up most of it, with a good number of trad lines and a little bouldering and top-roping. Grades run from about 5.6 to 5.11, with 5.10 the biggest group, and the few boulder problems are easy, V1 to V3. Mt Wells holds the most climbs and is one of the most popular crags in the area. It sits in forest, reached by a well-built trail, with short walk-ins to most walls and mostly sport routes. Rockfall is regular enough there that helmets are expected, and the trails can be slick after rain and icy in winter. Mt MacDonald and Glen Lake Crag come next by climb count, and Fleming Beach is a seaside spot for bouldering and top-roping.

co_bone_park_boulder_area.blurb: Bone Park is a bouldering-only area among the boulder fields on Nine Mile Hill in Unaweep Canyon, near Grand Junction. Those fields stretch along the highway for about nine miles and are spread across thousands of boulders, and Bone Park's problems are divided among many separate boulders and blocks, among them Guano Boulder, Minas Tirith Boulder and Jenga Boulder. Most problems fall between V0 and V4, with a thinner top end that reaches into double digits. In Unaweep Canyon generally, spring and fall have the mildest temperatures, shaded boulders can be climbed in summer, and crisp winter days can bring good friction.

ma_mt_spickett_goliath_rock_area.blurb: Mt. Spickett and Goliath Rock make up a bouldering area inside Lynn Woods, a municipal forest on the North Shore about ten miles north of Boston. Almost everything here is bouldering, with a single sport route. Problems run from very easy up to V9, but most sit between V0 and V4, so there is plenty for newer boulderers and a steady supply of harder lines. The area has a good concentration of problems and a short walk in, and first-time visitors to the woods often start here. Across Lynn Woods most boulders are coarse-grained granite left by glaciers. The Mt. Spickett area boulders hold the most climbs, with Goliath Rock, Golden Wall and Anvil Boulder among the other main stops.

mn_tettegouche_sp_north_shore.blurb: Tettegouche State Park lies on Minnesota's North Shore of Lake Superior near Silver Bay, and its climbing is on two cliffs above the lakeshore, Palisade Head and Shovel Point. Palisade Head holds the most climbs and is a headland cut off from the rest of the park. It formed from a very hard rhyolite lava flow. Trad is the main style, with top-rope lines, a few sport routes and a couple of ice climbs. Most routes fall between 5.8 and 5.12, with a handful of 5.13s and a thin base of easier climbs. Shovel Point has dozens of climbs, leaning toward top-roping. At both cliffs the routes are reached by rappelling in to lead them or top-roping from above.

nv_lower_canyon.blurb: Lower Canyon is the densest cluster of climbing in Keyhole Canyon, in the Eldorado Mountains of southern Nevada between Boulder City and Searchlight. The style is old-school trad: committing, sometimes run-out climbs with sparse bolts and no sport routes, on quartz monzonite coated in desert varnish. Gear placements can be hard to spot, and everything can be top-roped. Alongside the trad is a large bouldering scene, from V0 up into the V7 range, plus a few aid lines. Trad grades run from 5.2 to 5.11, mostly 5.6 to 5.10. Jimbo Rocks holds the most climbs, with First Waterfall Area and Front Bouldering Wall also among the larger spots. The area is hot six months of the year.
